Leveraging a lightweight rule-based reward (e.g., the similarity score between ground-truth and LLM-generated solutions), SWE-RL enables LLMs to autonomously recover a developer’s reasoning processes and solutions
We introduce SWE-RL, the first reinforcement learning (RL) approach to improve language models (LLMs) on software engineering tasks using software evolution data (e.g., PRs) and rule-based rewards.

Overall, our results suggest for the first time that reinforcement learning on real-world software data like PRs enables the model to acquire generalized reasoning skills, whereas supervised finetuning steers the language model towards a specific task distribution

First, our reward implementation compares the sequence similarity between the predicted and oracle patch rather than their semantic equivalence. This may prevent the policy LLM from exploring alternative, functional equivalent solutions.

This “external structure” prevents the model from learning through interaction feedback and hinders its ability to consider the entire problem holistically.
